method: Source-of-record check at authoring time, then a separate second pass re-reading every numeric and quoted claim against the page it came from. Author and checker are the same pass, which is not the independent arrangement the older batches used.

findings.claim: The seven defining constants and their exact values: dNuCs 9,192,631,770 Hz; c 299,792,458 m/s; h 6.62607015e-34 J s; e 1.602176634e-19 C; k 1.380649e-23 J/K; NA 6.02214076e23 per mole; Kcd 683 lm/W
Which units each constant helps define
The seven base unit definitions as currently written
Fixing a constant relocates uncertainty from the constant onto the artefact rather than reducing it
findings.sourceChecked: reasoning across the two NIST pages and the kilogram page
findings.note: Our framing. The NIST pages state the definitions; the inversion argument is ours and is written as an explanation.

findings.claim: The definitions are nested, and none prescribes an experiment
findings.note: Both observations follow from the definitions as printed; neither is quoted.

findings.claim: Atomic clocks count 9,192,631,770 microwave oscillations of caesium and call that a second
Commercially available caesium clocks keep time to within 1/3,000,000 of a second per year
New experimental clocks based on other atoms are ten thousand times more precise still
1/3,000,000 s per year is about one part in 10^14, and ten thousand times better is one part in 10^18
findings.note: Our conversion of the NIST figures; stated as approximate.

findings.claim: At one part in 10^18 a clock resolves the gravitational redshift over a few centimetres of height
findings.note: Standard consequence of general relativity at that fractional precision; no experiment is cited.

findings.claim: A clock error of a nanosecond is a position error of about 30 centimetres in satellite navigation
findings.sourceChecked: arithmetic on the speed of light
findings.note: Our arithmetic, using the defined value of c.

findings.claim: In 1954 the kelvin was defined as 1/273.16 of the thermodynamic temperature of the triple point of water
For a precise formulation of water at a specific pressure the triple point always occurs at exactly 273.16 K
The new definition fixes the Boltzmann constant at exactly 1.380649e-23 J/K, adopted with the revised SI in November 2018
Extrapolation from the water triple point to extreme temperatures was the weakness the redefinition addressed
A well-made triple-point cell realises the fixed point to better than a tenth of a millikelvin
findings.note: Standard metrological performance figure; not quoted from a page we read.

findings.claim: Acoustic, Johnson-noise and dielectric-constant gas thermometry are primary realisations of the redefined kelvin
For more than a century the kilogram was defined as the mass of a small polished platinum-iridium cylinder cast in 1879
The measured mass of each individual standard drifted a bit over time
In November 2018 the international scientific community voted to redefine the kilogram on a constant of nature
The kilogram is defined by fixing h at 6.62607015e-34 J s
Copies drifted by tens of micrograms over a century
findings.note: The page states that the standards drifted and that this created scaling problems; the magnitude is widely reported but is not on the page we read, so it is written as an approximate scale.

findings.claim: The Kibble balance and the silicon-sphere route are the two realisations
findings.note: Named as realisations without uncertainties; the page describes the shift to a constant rather than detailing either apparatus.

findings.claim: One mole contains exactly 6.02214076 x 10^23 elementary entities
The Avogadro constant equals 6.02214076 x 10^23 particles per mole and helps define the mole
The previous definition tied the mole to 12 grams of carbon-12, coupling it to the kilogram
findings.sourceChecked: not quoted from a page read in this pass
findings.note: The historical definition is standard; the NIST pages we read give the current definition only.

findings.claim: Molar masses are no longer exact by definition, with an uncertainty around one part in 10^9
findings.note: A known consequence of the redefinition; the magnitude is stated as approximate and no source is cited for it.

findings.claim: Avogadro's constant was determined by counting atoms in an isotopically enriched silicon-28 sphere
The caesium definition, the commercial clock performance and the margin held by experimental clocks
The Boltzmann and Avogadro values as fixed in the definitions
Electrical units are realised through the Josephson and quantum Hall effects, which depend only on h and e
findings.sourceChecked: not quoted from a page read in this pass
findings.note: Standard quantum electrical metrology; stated without figures. The NIST pages we read establish that e and h are fixed, not how the electrical realisations work.

findings.claim: Five of the seven base units are realised through quantum physics
findings.note: A count we make from the definitions rather than a claim any source states.

findings.claim: Atoms of a given species are identical, so a standard built on an atomic property needs no master copy
